hypothesis: Some true relationships remain separated by candidate-family boundaries. Selectively pooling a pair of HMM-supported families for a provisional joint gene tree may recover relationships while distinguishing duplications, without broad candidate expansion or unconditional global merging. Neither sequence similarity nor a supported tree guarantees correct orthology.
baseline: Frozen unweighted canonical high_sensitivity/satellite_v2 control, initial min4/cap100, BLOSUM62, CPM0.1/seed4, one original profile pass, default refinement, inferred min_variance species tree and species_overlap/positive_paralogy reconciliation with legacy support mapping. Upstream weighting and strict_span_guard interventions remain off. Span evidence is used only to validate local nominations, not to apply the separate global recruitment guard.
nomination: Read the complete validated original candidate partition, FASTA ownership and authenticated canonical initial HMM hit arrays. No reference orthogroups, QfO labels, GO/EC/FAS annotations, comparator predictions or dataset-specific inference rules may enter nomination or scoring.
Consider only source families with at least3 genes and2 species, and pairs with at most200 combined genes. Preserve complete original families; do not select individual favorable genes from them.

Aggregate accepted positive cross-species, cross-family initial HMM hits in bounded chunks. For each directed family pair retain the maximum existing normalized sequence-HMM score and up to two distinct query and target IDs as support witnesses. Require at least two distinct queries and targets in both directions. This is reciprocal family-level evidence, not a claim of reciprocal gene-pair identity.

For each supported unordered family pair, rank its score as the geometric mean of the two directional maxima. Nominate only unique mutual-best neighboring families. Exact best-score ties abstain; do not break a tie to manufacture support. Record the best competing neighbor, runner-up score and margin, including no-runner-up cases. Margins are descriptive, not calibrated orthology confidence, and there is no post-result margin sweep.

Mutual-best pairs are disjoint. Order eligible pairs by descending score, breaking equal pair-budget ranks by canonical sorted gene-name tuples, and analyze at most128 contexts. Record all ineligible, ambiguous and budget-excluded cases and the number of genes/families not examined. No transitive or iterated candidate union is permitted.
profile_validation: Build the existing unweighted multi-sequence profile separately for each of the two source families, retaining their members and original boundaries. Score each family's members against the opposite family profile without a second all-database candidate expansion. Use the existing original CPU Viterbi scorer, BLOSUM62 significance approximation and full-proteome database residue count; do not make significance more favorable by pretending the selected neighborhood is the whole database.

For significant cross-profile hits at E<1e-4, recover representative Viterbi spans and require exact raw integer score equality. Count known match-state residues, not bounding-span length. Profile support requires max(aligned model coverage, aligned target coverage)>=0.8, using the same fixed integer rule as the span implementation. Asymmetry is retained and reported; it is not asserted to be orthology, an identical domain architecture or a diagnosed fragment/fusion/fission.

Require supported targets from at least two genes and two species on each side. These criteria nominate a tree analysis only; they never create ortholog pairs or final OG memberships directly. Save scores, significance settings, spans, source profiles and all rejection reasons.
joint_tree_validation: Use the control's self-inferred global species tree as the provisional local reconciliation context, not a supplied benchmark/reference species tree. Infer a fresh MAFFT alignment and FastTree LG gene tree over the union of the two complete source families through OrthoHMM's existing _reconcile_family implementation. Keep the same rooting, pair and support-transport rules as the baseline. Save token mappings, inputs, raw/rooted/reconciled trees, checkpoints and tools/versions.

Apply the original source/target membership constraints belonging to these families through the existing high_confidence_pair policy before judging the local proposal. No new blanket satellite constraint or gene-name heuristic is introduced.

Require every existing baseline high-confidence native ortholog pair within the joint genes to remain present in the locally constrained result. Require new high-confidence cross-boundary pairs involving at least two genes and two species from each source family, with both genes also in a common local root group. High means the existing reconciliation class, not a new branch-support cutoff or a calibrated truth probability.

Only after these gates pass may the pair become one effective candidate context for the final native pipeline. Otherwise retain both original candidates. Original OGs are not globally replaced during nomination, and there is no merge-until-convergence loop.
final_inference_and_semantics: Write a complete unique effective candidate partition reflecting only accepted disjoint pair contexts. Preserve all unrelated families and the original membership-constraint gene sets; validate that each original constraint remains inside one effective candidate. If no proposal is accepted, preserve the original candidate bytes exactly.

Run the ordinary native inferred-species-tree and reconciliation pipeline on this effective partition with unchanged membership/root/pair policies. Reuse only exact-compatible baseline or provisional joint raw-tree checkpoints with authenticated input/raw-tree hashes and explicit provenance. The final species tree may differ from the provisional control tree; report that fact rather than claiming it was held fixed or that provisional preservation guarantees final monotonicity.

Generate official groups, native pairs, confidence, event records and counts through the native writers. Do not manually append rescued pairs, silently change pair/group semantics, or substitute context trees with incompatible leaf/token sets. Validate complete gene ownership and every exported pair against its effective candidate.

Report separately the numbers of candidate contexts joined, final root-OG membership changes, new/lost native pairs and confidence classes, baseline-pair preservation in the provisional versus final stage, and all zero-activation/zero-acceptance outcomes. A nominal group or functional score gain is not proof that the local tree alone caused improvement.
implementation_scope: Implement label-independent reusable nomination/proposal functions in the OrthoHMM package and an experimental workflow driver using the existing native pipeline. Pilot this explicit cached-baseline/proposal/final-native workflow before any default or broader production integration. If promising, finish a tested opt-in production interface and full-vector confirmation before recommending it; a negative prototype remains clearly experimental.
evaluation: Test chunk and input-order invariance, exact unique-neighbor/tie rules, witness counts, family/species/gene bounds, disjointness, deterministic budget ordering, unsupported inputs and empty/inactive cases. Runtime labels are generated family membership/FASTA ownership or baseline model outputs only.

Test real two-family HMM validation and raw-score/span equality. Test controlled speciation, ancient duplication, uncertain mapping, changed membership constraints and baseline-pair-loss cases. A homology-only or paralogy case must not create a proposal. Include actual MAFFT/FastTree/local reconciliation integration and exact cache compatibility/ownership checks.

Run a label-free applicability probe before accuracy scoring, in fixed priority OrthoBench then corrected QfO then Three Kingdoms if earlier datasets have no analyzable context. Do not retune to force activation. If all are inactive, document the bounded applicability result without presenting it as biological accuracy validation.

For the primary OrthoBench pilot, require an exact unchanged off control and independently verified nonempty method activation before interpreting an active local_joint_v1 result. Score official OG precision, recall and F1 independently, and report native-pair turnover separately rather than calling a pair metric OrthoBench OG F1.

An active OrthoBench arm advances only if OG F1 strictly increases and neither precision nor recall falls by more than0.005. If it fails, close this fixed branch without retuning. If OrthoBench is inactive, any prespecified applicability fallback is a separately labeled diagnostic, not an invented passing OrthoBench gate.

For an advancing arm, execute unchanged settings on complete corrected QfO and Three Kingdoms, report the full eight-endpoint vector with precision/recall/populations/resources and appropriate uncertainty, and seek post-freeze confirmation if available. Keep TreeFam supporting, Three Kingdoms supplementary, all existing panels development-exposed and unrun endpoints explicitly NA. Missing independent confirmation limits claims rather than blocking completion.

resources.timing: Separate baseline replay, nomination, profile validation, local tree and final native costs; shared-host descriptive timing, not isolated full-pipeline runtime

literature_context.title: OrthoFinder: phylogenetic orthology inference for comparative genomics (2019)
literature_context.scope: Supports gene/species-tree reconciliation as orthology evidence, not the correctness or expected gain of this proposed local rule.

literature_context.title: Domainoid: domain-oriented orthology inference (2019)
literature_context.scope: Motivates treating shared domains and architecture changes cautiously; no domain annotation from this benchmark is used at runtime.

git: Commit and push this protocol before implementation/evaluation; then push focused tested package/workflow, frozen manifests, results and decisions. Preserve running weighting/alignment source trees, original failures, raw artifacts and unrelated user changes.
